chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever builds a mosque, Allah builds for him a house in Paradise.' Abu Ubaydah said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) passed by me on the road to Mecca, and I had arranged stones for a mosque. I said: 'May I be your ransom, we hope that this will be from that.' He said: 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for building a mosque according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the spiritual merit of mosque construction as a tangible act of worship, linking physical effort to eternal reward. The narrative context, where Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) personally affirms the reward upon seeing the physical preparation of stones, underscores the Shia emphasis on the sincerity and tangible nature of charitable deeds (sadaqah jariyah). It highlights the Imam's role in validating the spiritual status of believers' practical contributions to communal worship spaces.
